conversations.title: Why disabled people are turning to specialist dating apps
conversations.reply: It's great that people are finding ways to connect that work for them, and it's about time we had spaces where disability isn't a dealbreaker, but just a part of who you are.

conversations.title: How two sisters built a dating app for people with disabilities ,  then received a special wedding invitation
conversations.reply: Taking the pressure off disclosure can be a huge relief, and it's amazing when people can just be themselves from the start, no awkwardness or fear of being ghosted.

conversations.title: Interabled Dating: Building a Relationship Without a Caregiver Dynamic
conversations.reply: It's fantastic to see people talking about interabled relationships in a way that's about mutual respect and understanding, every relationship is unique and that's what makes them special.

conversations.title: Scotch Plains Celebrates Disability Pride Month With Inclusive Play in the Park
conversations.reply: That sounds like a fantastic event, it's wonderful to see inclusive spaces like this where everyone can relax and enjoy themselves without any barriers.

conversations.title: Imperial Takeover @ Heaven
conversations.reply: It's brilliant that events like this are thinking about accessibility, and it's a great start that they're checking in with the venue, hopefully more events will follow their lead.

conversations.title: disabled audiences
conversations.reply: Venues that take accessibility seriously are on the right track, but it's not just about training, it's about creating a space where everyone can feel at home.

conversations.title: App feature allows deaf festivalgoers to book BSL interpreters for Fringe shows
conversations.reply: Features like this are a great start, and it's amazing that deaf festivalgoers can book BSL interpreters, but there's still so much to be done to make festivals truly inclusive.

conversations.title: kingshouseconf
conversations.reply: That's really great to hear about Kings House, it's so helpful when venues are open to making things work for everyone.

TARGETS: 10 replies on X and 5 comments on Instagram, found and posted a few at a time (pause whenever I say pause). Skip and tell me if we run out of genuinely good candidates; never pad with weak ones.

FINDING CANDIDATES:
- X: use x.com search (Latest tab) for: disability dating, dating with a disability, accessible venue, wheelchair nightlife, #DisabilityDating, #DisabledAndDating, chronic illness dating, plus anything matching today's ammo below. Real people only: skip news outlets, brands, giveaways, and anything about death, grief, tragedy or self-harm.

React to what each post actually is: agree and back people up when they've had a rough time, help when they ask, be glad for them when they celebrate. Usually 1 to 2 short sentences on X, shorter is fine for IG. UK English. NEVER use an em dash or en dash. Disability is never the punchline. Never invent facts, studies, numbers, or claims about any venue, person, company, or the app's features. Never argue; skip hostile threads. Never preachy or lecturing: no "access should be the baseline", "legal requirement", "not a favour", "stark reminder", "raising awareness", "it's time to". Never negative at the person.
